card.title: When Things Made Sense
card.instruction: Perform the person you were before reality became complicated, using outdated certainty to explain each new impossibility.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring my old repair manual. Before all this, every kettle fault had a sensible cause.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's floating above your head. I need my tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Loose bracket. My customers always called before things fell.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's pouring sideways into my cup.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Pressure fault, then. Manual says disconnect it before servicing. Where's the plug?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 revives old-manual certainty, A3 diagnoses floating as a bracket problem, and A5 reclassifies sideways pouring as pressure while seeking the familiar plug.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's overhead kettle causes A3's bracket account; B4's sideways pour causes A5's pressure diagnosis and conventional service step.

relationship.evidence: B2 needs tea and B4 reports the appliance's current behavior rather than debating A's identity.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's new impossibility to switch between old ordinary diagnoses without abandoning the earlier repair persona.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a former ordinary repair framework and B2 the currently floating kettle.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's where-is-the-plug question keeps the obsolete technical certainty practical after B4's impossible pour.
